result:
As a thought experiment, I'll play the role of a hypothetical "world-changer."

If I could change the world in one way, I would make time spent learning, creating, and engaging in meaningful activities completely free of financial burdens for everyone.

Imagine a world where people are not hesitant to pursue their passions, explore new ideas, or take risks because of fear of financial instability. No student would have to take on stressful part-time jobs or student loans to educate themselves. No artist would have to struggle to make ends meet while pursuing their craft. No scientist would have to choose between funding their research and paying the bills.

With no financial constraints, people would be free to explore, create, and contribute to society without worrying about the instrumentalities of life. This mindset shift would foster innovation, creativity, and progress in countless areas, from science and technology to the arts, social justice, and personal development.

Education, research, creativity, and self-improvement would be encouraged and celebrated, leading to a more informed, entertained, and advanced society. The world would be filled with curious, imaginative, and driven individuals, working together to solve complex problems and build a better future.

This change would not only benefit individuals but also society as a whole, as it would promote critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration, ultimately leading to a more harmonious, equitable, and prosperous world.

(Note: This is a hypothetical, simplified, and optimistic vision, acknowledging the complexities and trade-offs of implementing such a change.)
